exposure: Maximal maternal temperature (classified into 5 ordinal levels)
Duration from fever onset to delivery
cohort: The study included nonanomalous singleton neonates born at or after 35 weeks gestational age to laboring mothers at 15 Kaiser Permanente Northern California hospitals between 2012 and 2019, excluding those born by elective cesarean section.
finding: The risk of neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy increases with higher maternal temperature and longer duration from fever onset to delivery, even after adjusting for labor duration.
